land.text: Antigonus's share of Alexander's empire, 'Greece, Asia Minor, Syria, Phoenicia and northern Mesopotamia', made a kingdom when 'Antigonus assumed the title of king' in 306

predecessors.note: Cliopatria draws Antigonus's Asia inside its 'Macedonian Empire' shape of 307-302; that dossier subtracts it from 306.

land.text: Macedon, Thessaly and the Antipatrid garrisons in Greece, taken by Demetrius Poliorcetes in 294

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's Antigonid Dynasty row begins in 291; the Demetrius I page dates the seizure of the throne to 294.

land.text: Macedon, 'divided into four merides' (Amphipolis, Thessalonica, Pella, Pelagonia) in 167 as Roman client republics, a province from 146

successors.note: The four republics are Roman clients (rule 4 tint under the roman-republic dossier) until the province of 146 BC; Andriscus's revolt (150-148) is the Roman dossier's rebel.

capitals.name: Antigoneia on the Orontes
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Antigoneia (Antigonus I)'; coronation at Antigoneia in 306 (Antigonus I page). Between Ipsus (301) and 294 Demetrius had no fixed seat.

capitals.name: Demetrias (Volos)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Demetrias (Demetrius I)'; in 280 Ptolemy Keraunos 'confined him [Antigonus II] to the city of Demetrias, Thessaly'. Pella, the Macedonian capital, was Demetrius's seat in 294-288 as king of Macedon.

capitals.name: Pella
capitals.note: Infobox 'Pella (since Antigonus II)'; the Macedonia page: 'Pella 399-168 BC'.

rulers.name: Demetrius I Poliorcetes
rulers.note: King of Macedon 294-288 (the dynasty table gives 294-287); surrendered to Seleucus and 'died after a confinement of three years (283 BC)'.

rulers.name: Antigonus II Gonatas
rulers.note: Antigonid king 283-239; king of Macedon 277-274 and 272-239 (in 274-272 'only the coastal areas' against Pyrrhus); the dynasty table gives 276-239.

rulers.name: Perseus
rulers.note: Succeeded 'on 22 June 179 BC'; defeated at Pydna 22 June 168; died at Alba Fucens in 166.

union.text: Asia Minor without the Armenian Highlands and the Orontid kingdom's outline (Cliopatria's Kingdom of Armenia, 307-302), where the Orontids ruled as kings (Orontid page: 'the Macedonians never established firm control over the country')

correction.text: Antigonus's kingdom at his coronation, for 306-305: 'Greece, Asia Minor, Syria, Phoenicia and northern Mesopotamia' (Antigonus I page), Cyprus 'conquered that year' (306) and Athens, taken by Demetrius in 307; Corinth, Boeotia and Euboea only from 304 (new keyframe -304); without the Armenian Highlands of the Orontid kingdom

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Antigonid shape before 291 and draws this kingdom inside 'Macedonian Empire' 307-302 (1.53 M km2 with Cassander's Macedon). Lysimachus 'crossed over the Hellespont in 302 BC' and Ptolemy took Coele-Syrian cities the same year: contest events in the ledger. Fix run: ended at 305, because Corinth and the cities of the Corinthian League are a 304-303 gain (Demetrius I page: 'In 304-303 he seized cities including Corinth'), and in 306-305 they are Cassander's (macedonian-empire loses them in 304). fx-29 (F150): Armenian Highlands and Cliopatria's Kingdom of Armenia outline (307-302) cut from the Asia Minor part (Orontid dynasty page: 'the Macedonians never established firm control over the country'; the Antigonus I page's list of his realm does not name Armenia).

union.text: Asia Minor without the Armenian Highlands and the Orontid kingdom's outline (Cliopatria's Kingdom of Armenia, 307-302), where the Orontids ruled as kings (Orontid page: 'the Macedonians never established firm control over the country')

correction.text: the 306 kingdom with Corinth, Boeotia and Euboea, the Greek cities Demetrius took in 304-303 and 'reinstated' in the Corinthian League; without the Armenian Highlands of the Orontid kingdom

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: backs the 304 gain from macedonian-empire (ledger). The macedonian-empire dossier ends its 307 correction at 305 and subtracts the same cities from 304. fx-29 (F150): Armenian Highlands and Cliopatria's Kingdom of Armenia outline (307-302) cut from the Asia Minor part (Orontid dynasty page: 'the Macedonians never established firm control over the country'; the Antigonus I page's list of his realm does not name Armenia).

correction.text: what Demetrius kept after Ipsus: Cyprus (until Ptolemy's reconquest in 295/294) and Corinth, seized in 304-303; Boeotia is not drawn (ledger loss c. 301, confidence 1: no page places it in his hands before the revolt and retaking of Thebes in 291); Athens 'refused to admit him' in 301 and was retaken only in 294

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe at confidence 1: the pages opened say only that Demetrius 'retired to Ephesus' and 'sailed for Greece'. Cyprus stays until 295/294 on the Ptolemy I Soter page ('reconquered Cyprus in 295/294'; ledger loss 294). Boeotia was dropped in the fix run: the Demetrius page has only the rebellion and 'capturing Thebes in 291 BC', which the ledger records as a 291 gain from the Boeotian League, so Boeotia cannot also be held continuously 301-295. Tyre and Sidon are not on any page opened. Cliopatria's Macedonian row of 301-292 carries Cyprus too (macedonian-empire subtracts it).

correction.text: Demetrius's Macedon, Thessaly and Greece from 294, when he 'established himself on the throne of Macedonia by murdering Alexander V': the same shape Cliopatria draws from 291

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the Antigonid row starts three years late.

correction.text: the shape as drawn, but only to 288: Pyrrhus, Ptolemy and Lysimachus 'obliged him to leave Macedonia in 288 BC'; from 288 (287 on the Lysimachus page) Macedon is divided between Lysimachus and Pyrrhus and the Antigonids keep the Greek holdings of the 284 shape

keyframe_review.note: 127,922 km2 for 291-285, bbox 19.3-24.3 E: Macedon with Thessaly, Boeotia (Thebes retaken 291) and the garrisons in Greece. The new keyframe antigonid-dynasty_-287 below gives the shape for 287-285.

correction.text: the Greek holdings Demetrius 'left Antigonus in control of' after losing Macedon: the Peloponnesian and Euboean garrisons with Corinth, Chalcis and Piraeus, and Demetrias in Thessaly

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria keeps Macedon in the Antigonid shape to 285 although Lysimachus and Pyrrhus held it from 288/287 (Lysimachus's own row shows Macedon only from 283). Athens revolted c. 287 ('Meanwhile, Athens revolted', undated) and is not inside.

25,373 km2 for 284-282, bbox 21.2-24.2 E and 36.9-39.1 N: the Peloponnesian and Euboean garrisons of Antigonus Gonatas, 'the rest of Greece'. Demetrias (39.37 N) lies just outside the bbox although the page puts Antigonus there in 280.

36,828 km2 for 281-280, bbox north to 40.2 N: the Greek holdings with Demetrias and the Magnesian coast, where Ptolemy Keraunos 'defeated him in a naval battle and confined him to the city of Demetrias, Thessaly'.

23,235 km2 for 279-278: the Greek garrisons during the Gallic invasion (Brennus at Thermopylae and Delphi, 279). Macedon itself, under Meleager, Antipater Etesias and Sosthenes (279-277), has no Cliopatria shape at all in these years (notes).

137,606 km2 for 277-273, bbox 19.3-28.3 E: Macedon ('By the end of 276 BC Antigonus had gained control of most of Macedon' after Lysimachia, 277), Thessaly and the Greek garrisons, reaching the Thracian Chersonese at Lysimachia. Pyrrhus 'took control of upper Macedonia and Thessaly' in 274: a ledger loss inside this span, restored in 272.

60,364 km2 for 272 only: 'Pyrrhus now took control of upper Macedonia and Thessaly, while Antigonus held on to the coastal towns'. Cliopatria dates the reduced shape to 272 although Pyrrhus held the interior from 274; after his death at Argos in 272 'his whole army and camp surrendered to Antigonus'.
116,032 km2 for 271-265: Macedon, Thessaly and the garrisons, through the first years of the Chremonidean War (from 267; Areus of Sparta killed outside Corinth in 265).

105,544 km2 for 264-257. Athens 'starved into surrender in either 262 BC or 261 BC' and garrisoned: vassal tint over Attica from 261 (ledger). Cliopatria's 'Athenian Coalition' shape of 264-257 overlaps this one at Attica and Laconia.

128,306 km2 for 256-248, bbox west to 19.2 E: the shape reaches the Epirote and Illyrian coast, which none of the pages opened explains (no Macedonian gain in Epirus or Illyria is recorded for these years). Unverified; kept as drawn and flagged in notes. The revolt of Alexander of Corinth (c. 253-245) takes Corinth out of Macedonian hands inside this span (ledger).
114,795 km2 for 247-240: Corinth recovered 'in the winter of 245/44 BC' and lost to Aratus in 243 ('seized the Acrocorinth'): ledger.
117,101 km2 for 239-231: Demetrius II's kingdom, which 'extended into Euboea, Magnesia, and Thessaly'; Boeotia submitted in 236 (vassal tint).
101,306 km2 for 230-226: after Demetrius II's death (229) the Athenian forts were surrendered by Diogenes and Argos joined the Achaeans (229); Doson defeated the Dardani.

93,179 km2 for 225-217: Doson's kingdom; 'Acrocorinth, Corinth, Heraea, and Orchomenus went to Macedon' (224-223, ledger), Sellasia 222, and in the Social War 'Triphylia and Phthiotis went to Macedon' (219-217).
93,373 km2 for 216-213: the first Illyrian attempts (216 aborted, fleet lost 214, Oricum and Apollonia 214) take no lasting ground.
108,962 km2 for 212-211, bbox west to 19.7 E: Lissus (213) and 'Dassaretis, Atintani and Parthini, and the town of Dimale' (213-212).
112,456 km2 for 210-209, bbox to 19.3 E: the Illyrian conquests at their widest; the Aetolians and Romans take Anticyra (210) and Aegina is sold to Attalus.
112,066 km2 for 208-207: Echinus 'invested and took' by Philip; Thermon raided again c. 207.

111,039 km2 for 206-204: the Aetolians 'sued for a separate peace' in 206; at Phoenice (205) 'Rome would control the Parthinians, Dimallum, Bargulum, and Eugenium' and Macedon Atintania: the ledger removes the Parthini and Dimale in 205.
112,593 km2 for 203 only: the Cretan War years; no border change on the pages.

114,371 km2 for 202-198: Philip's Aegean and Carian campaign (Samos besieged, Miletus captured, Caria invaded, Chios and Lade 201, Abydos 200) is a ledger gain of Carian footholds in 201, lost in the 196 peace; the shape does not reach Caria (bbox 28.3 E), so the Asian footholds are left to the ledger.

50,097 km2 for 197-171: Macedon after Cynoscephalae (June 197), when 'Macedonia gives up all possessions and client states in Orestis, Thessaly, southern Greece, Thrace and Anatolia'. The Thessalian, Perrhaebian and Athamanian towns Philip occupied in 191 and later gave up are ledger events (191 gain, 185 loss at confidence 1); the shape's bbox east to 29.6 E (the Chersonese: Aenus and Maronea) is unexplained by the pages opened.

correction.text: the shape as drawn, but only to June 168: 'decisively defeated the Macedonian forces at the Battle of Pydna in 168 BC' (22 June 168, Pydna infobox); in 167 'Macedon was to be divided into four merides'

keyframe_review.note: 43,431 km2 for 170-165, bbox 20.8-24.0 E: Macedon proper. Cliopatria keeps the kingdom to 165; the three extra years are the Roman client republics (roman-republic dossier). The Molossians who 'went over to the Macedonians' in 170 are vassal tint (ledger), not Antigonid territory.

union.text: Asia Minor without the Armenian Highlands and the Orontid kingdom's outline (Cliopatria's Kingdom of Armenia, 307-302), where the Orontids ruled as kings (Orontid page: 'the Macedonians never established firm control over the country')

region.text: 'Greece, Asia Minor, Syria, Phoenicia and northern Mesopotamia' and Cyprus

ledger.note: 306: Antigonus takes the title of king. After Demetrius's victory at Salamis in Cyprus 'Antigonus assumed the title of king'; the Antigonid dynasty page's infobox 'Established: 306 BC'. The nominal Macedonian empire's Asian half becomes a kingdom of its own; Athens had been Demetrius's since 307. fx-29 (F150): the Armenian Highlands and Cliopatria's Kingdom of Armenia outline of 307-302 are cut from the Asia Minor part (30 cells at the Tigris edge of 'northern Mesopotamia' still overlap the Armenian outline; the pages do not settle them and the size rule keeps them with Armenia). The Orontid dynasty page: Neoptolemus 'seems to have failed to take control of the country', 'the Macedonians never established firm control over the country', 'the Orontids ruled as kings in practice'; the Antigonus I page lists 'Greece, Asia Minor, Syria, Phoenicia and northern Mesopotamia' and never names Armenia. The kingdom-of-armenia dossier has held the Armenian Highlands since 331 (537 cells were drawn twice in 306 and 304).

region.text: Cyprus, taken from Ptolemy after Salamis

ledger.note: 306: Cyprus conquered. Demetrius 'defeated Ptolemy at Salamis' and 'also conquered Cyprus that year, capturing one of Ptolemy's sons'.

region.text: Corinth and the Greek cities of the revived Corinthian League

ledger.note: 304-303: Demetrius 'returned a second time to Greece as liberator, and reinstated the Corinthian League'; 'In 304-303 he seized cities including Corinth'. The siege of Rhodes (305-304) had failed.

region.text: the Peloponnesian cities of Polyperchon's command

ledger.note: 303: Demetrius reverses Polyperchon's Peloponnese. 'In 303 BC, Demetrius Poliorcetes launched a campaign in Greece and quickly reversed many of Polyperchon's gains' (Polyperchon page). Mirrors polyperchon's 303 loss to this state (the same region).

region.text: Asia Minor, invaded by Lysimachus, and Coele-Syria, where Ptolemy 'captured cities' and garrisoned them

ledger.note: 302: the coalition invades. 'Lysimachus crossed over the Hellespont in 302 BC', 'reinforced by troops from Cassander', and 'met with little resistance' (Lysimachus page); Seleucus marched from the east.

region.text: Asia Minor and Syria, settled at Ipsus

ledger.note: 301: Ipsus. 'Antigonus died during the battle in his eighty-first year after being struck by a javelin'; 'The empire was carved up between the victors'.

region.text: 'Lydia, Ionia, Phrygia and the north coast of Asia Minor', Lysimachus's share

ledger.note: 301: western Asia Minor to Lysimachus ('Lysimachus receiving the remainder of Asia Minor', Ipsus page).

region.text: eastern Asia Minor, Syria and northern Mesopotamia, Seleucus's share

ledger.note: 301: Syria and the east of Anatolia to Seleucus ('Seleucus expanding his power to eastern Asia Minor'; Syria is the Diadochi page's reading). Cilicia went to Cassander's brother Pleistarchus on the usual account, which no page opened confirms.

region.text: Coele-Syria, whose cities Ptolemy 'captured' in 302 and 'garrisoned'

ledger.note: 301: Ptolemy keeps Coele-Syria. He 'captured cities there in 302 BC, then garrisoned them and withdrew into Egypt after receiving false reports'; the Ipsus page does not say he kept them, the Diadochi page does not assign them; the Ptolemaic dossier should settle it (Tyre and Sidon stayed Demetrius's on the usual account).

region.text: Athens, which 'refused to admit him'

ledger.note: 301: Athens closes its gates. After Ipsus Demetrius 'retired to Ephesus' and 'The Athenians then refused to admit him'.

region.text: Boeotia, held since 304 and not among what Demetrius kept after Ipsus on any page opened

ledger.note: 301-291: Boeotia leaves Demetrius's hands. The Demetrius page has only 'He faced rebellion from the Boeotians but secured the region after capturing Thebes in 291 BC' (below); no page dates the loss, so it is bridged to Ipsus at confidence 1 and keyframe 301-295 no longer draws Boeotia.

region.text: Athens, 'after a blockade'

ledger.note: 294: Athens retaken. 'He took Athens after a blockade.'

region.text: Macedon, Thessaly and the Antipatrid garrisons

ledger.note: 294: Demetrius king of Macedon. 'In the same year he established himself on the throne of Macedonia by murdering Alexander V, the son of Cassander.' The Antipatrid kingdom ends (macedonian-empire dossier).

region.text: Cyprus, taken by Demetrius in 306

ledger.note: 295/294: Ptolemy retakes Cyprus. Ptolemy 'lost what he held in Greece, but reconquered Cyprus in 295/294' (Ptolemy I Soter page; the Demetrius I page is silent). Mirrors the 306 gain; Cliopatria's Macedonian row of 301-292 still carries the island, which macedonian-empire now subtracts.

region.text: Boeotia, 'after capturing Thebes in 291 BC'

ledger.note: 291: Thebes retaken. Demetrius faced Boeotian rebellion and secured the region 'after capturing Thebes in 291 BC'; the Boeotians had been inside his Greek league since 304.

region.text: eastern and Lower Macedonia, Lysimachus's share

ledger.note: 288: Demetrius driven from Macedon. Pyrrhus, Ptolemy and Lysimachus 'obliged him to leave Macedonia in 288 BC'; 'Lysimachus and Pyrrhus divided Macedonia' (Macedonia page); the Lysimachus page dates the invasion to 287. The line between the two shares is the researcher's reading (Lysimachus the east, Pyrrhus the west). [Reviewer eu-02-a, 2026-10-18: region Ancient Macedon (Central plus Western Macedonia) narrowed to Central Macedonia: Western Macedonia is Pyrrhus's share in /ledger/13 and in kingdom-of-epirus /ledger/10, and kingdom-of-lysimachus /ledger/14 gains Central Macedonia.]

region.text: Upper Macedonia, Pyrrhus's share (approximated by Western Macedonia, as in kingdom-of-epirus)

ledger.note: 288: Pyrrhus and Lysimachus 'decided to share rulership over Macedonia'; Pyrrhus kept his share until 'In 284 BC, he was driven out of Macedon by Lysimachus' (285 on the Lysimachus page). kingdom-of-epirus gains Western Macedonia only. Fix run: North Macedonia dropped from the region, because kingdom-of-paeonia draws it as independent and this state never held it as Macedon's own land in 288.

region.text: Thessaly apart from Demetrias and the Magnesian coast

ledger.note: 288 (bridged): Thessaly leaves Demetrius with his Macedon. The Pyrrhus page names Pyrrhus, not Lysimachus, as its next holder: Antigonus Gonatas 'ceded Thessaly to him in order to make peace' (undated, after 286) and 'he ruled an enlarged Epirus, half of Macedonia, and Thessaly'. The year is kept at 288 because Cliopatria's 284 shape (kept in the 287-285 keyframe) no longer holds Thessaly; the real cession may be 286-285. Chain: antigonid-dynasty to kingdom-of-epirus (here), kingdom-of-epirus to kingdom-of-lysimachus (285). The Antigonid shape of 281-280 keeps only Demetrias, where Antigonus was 'confined' in 280.

region.text: Athens, which revolted against the garrison

ledger.note: c. 287: Athens revolts. 'Meanwhile, Athens revolted' (undated on the page; the revolt is usually placed in 287); Piraeus stayed Macedonian on the usual account, which the page does not say.

region.text: Macedon, 'most of' it by the end of 276

ledger.note: 277: Lysimachia and the Macedonian throne. 'In 277 BC, Antigonus II Gonatas defeated the Gauls at the Battle of Lysimachia' (Gallic invasion page); 'In 277 BC Antigonus organized an expedition to take Macedon from' Sosthenes (Lysimachia page); 'By the end of 276 BC Antigonus had gained control of most of Macedon'. Macedon's rulers of 281-277 (Ptolemy Keraunos, Meleager, Antipater Etesias, Sosthenes) have no Cliopatria row (notes).
277/276: the court returns to Pella ('Pella (since Antigonus II)').

region.text: Aegium (Aigio)

ledger.note: c. 275: Aegium expels the Macedonian garrison. 'Around the year 275 BC, the people expelled the Macedonian garrison and the city joined the new Achaean League' (Aigio page). Mirrors achaean-league's 275 gain; 'around' keeps the confidence at 2.

region.text: 'upper Macedonia and Thessaly', taken by Pyrrhus

ledger.note: 274: Pyrrhus's second conquest. 'Pyrrhus now took control of upper Macedonia and Thessaly, while Antigonus held on to the coastal towns'; 'Pyrrhus seized the Macedonian throne from Antigonus II Gonatas in 274 BC' (Pyrrhus page). Cliopatria shows the reduced shape only in 272. (Fix run: North Macedonia dropped from the region, as in 288: Paeonia was independent.)

region.text: upper Macedonia and Thessaly, recovered after Pyrrhus's death at Argos

ledger.note: 272: Pyrrhus killed at Argos; 'his whole army and camp surrendered to Antigonus, greatly increasing his power'. The king list gives Antigonus's second reign from 272. (Fix run: North Macedonia dropped from the region, as in 288: Paeonia was independent.)

region.text: Attica and the Isthmus, where Areus was killed outside Corinth in 265

ledger.note: 267: the Chremonidean War. Declared 'possibly as early as the autumn of 268 BC'; the war 'began in 267 BC'; 'a coalition of Greek city-states and Ptolemaic Egypt against Antigonid Macedonia'. The coalition is polities/chremonidean-alliance.json (split from Cliopatria's 'Athenian Coalition' row).

region.text: Attica

ledger.note: 262/261: Athens starved out. 'Athens had already been starved into surrender in either 262 BC or 261 BC'; infobox 'Macedonian victory' that 'confirmed Antigonid control over Greece'.

region.text: Athens under Macedonian garrisons

ledger.note: 261-229: Athens as a Macedonian dependency (rule 4 tint). The Gonatas page: 'the Athenians and Spartans... made peace with Antigonus, who thus retained his hold on Greece'; the forts were held by the garrison commander Diogenes until 229 (Aratus page).

region.text: Corinth and the Acrocorinth, under the rebel governor Alexander

ledger.note: c. 253: Alexander of Corinth revolts, 'the most serious threat to the Macedonian hegemony in Greece'. The page gives no start year (usually c. 253/252); Antigonus 'regained control of Corinth in the winter of 245/44 BC'.

region.text: Corinth

ledger.note: Winter 245/244: Corinth recovered.

region.text: Corinth and the Acrocorinth, 'the strategically important fort by which Antigonus controlled the Isthmus of Corinth'

ledger.note: 243: Aratus takes the Acrocorinth. 'Aratus' greatest success came when he captured Corinth and the fortress of Acrocorinth in 243 BC.'

region.text: Boeotia, whose cities 'submit immediately'

ledger.note: 236: Boeotia submits. 'In 236 BC, he invaded Boeotia, making the Boeotians submit immediately.' The Boeotians are still on Philip's side at Phoenice (205); the relation ends with the 196 settlement.

region.text: Athens, whose forts the garrison commander surrendered

ledger.note: 229: Athens freed. After Demetrius II's death Aratus succeeded in 'persuading the commander of the Macedonian garrison, Diogenes, to surrender' the Athenian forts.

region.text: Argos and the Argolid, whose tyrant 'abandoned the Macedonian alliance and joined the Achaean League'

ledger.note: 229: Argos goes over to the Achaeans ('Argos in 229 BC', Achaean League page). Argos lies at 22.72 E 37.63 N, about 35 km east of Tripoli; the gazetteer has no Argos, so the radius is drawn from Tripoli and should be replaced by 'Argolis' when the gazetteer gains it.

region.text: southern Paeonia (Gevgelija and Strumica, a reading)

ledger.note: 227: Antigonus Doson conquers southern Paeonia. 'In 227 BC, Antigonus Doson conquered the southern part of Paeonia, also called "Macedonian Paeonia"' (Paeonia page). Mirrors kingdom-of-paeonia's 227 loss; the extent is the other dossier's reading.

region.text: the Isthmus, the Argolid and Arcadia, fought over with Cleomenes

ledger.note: 224: Doson enters the Cleomenean War. Aratus 'invited Antigonus to intervene (226 BC)' (Doson page); the Achaeans 'were obliged to surrender the citadel overlooking Corinth to Antigonus in return for his help'; the Hellenic league reconstituted 'probably 224 BC'. Sparta needs a dossier (notes).

region.text: the Acrocorinth and Corinth

ledger.note: 224: Acrocorinth ceded to Macedon. Infobox territorial changes: 'Acrocorinth, Corinth, Heraea, and Orchomenus went to Macedon'; Antigonus 'occupied the Acrocorinth and put a garrison in the city' after Cleomenes left the Isthmus (Aratus page). The year is the Doson page's for the Hellenic league; the handover is usually 224.

region.text: Orchomenus and Heraea in Arcadia

ledger.note: 223: 'Antigonus proceeded to capture Mantinea, Heraea, and Telphusa, which confined Cleomenes to Laconia'; Heraea and Orchomenus 'went to Macedon' (infobox), Mantinea to the Achaeans.

region.text: the Peloponnese

ledger.note: July 222: Sellasia. Cleomenes 'was defeated at the Battle of Sellasia in July 222 BC, and fled to Egypt'; 'Antigonus entered Sparta triumphantly, its first foreign conqueror' but did not annex it (Cleomenean War page).

region.text: Aetolia, Elis and Triphylia

ledger.note: 219: Philip's campaigns in the Social War. 'In 219, Philip took Aetolian-held towns in western Aetolia, including Elaeus and Oeniadae'; 'In the winter of 219/18, he marched through Arcadia and Elis into Triphylia, where he took Psophis and Lasion'; Thermon raided in 218.

region.text: Triphylia, south of the Alpheus (Zacharo and Lepreon)

ledger.note: Winter 219/218: Triphylia taken. Social War page: 'Next he fought the Aetolians in Triphylia'; infobox 'Triphylia and Phthiotis to Macedon, Psophis and Lasion to Achaea'; the Elean leader Amphidamus. Triphylia was Elean territory with Aetolian help, and aetolian-league never draws it, so the counterpart is Elis (the name achaean-league uses for Psophis and Lasion) instead of the Aetolian League; fix run: the disc is recentred south of the Alpheus, since a Pirgos 40 km circle lies in Elis proper.

region.text: Oeniadae and Elaeus at the mouth of the Acheloos

ledger.note: 219: Philip takes Oeniadae and Elaeus. 'he conquered several cities, including Elaeus and Oeniadae' (Social War page, summer 219). Mirrors aetolian-league's 219 loss (the same region).

region.text: Phthiotic Thebes and Phthiotis

ledger.note: 217: Phthiotic Thebes taken ('Philip took the city of Thebes in Phthiotic Achaea'); the peace of Naupactus (217) let 'every side... maintain what it currently possessed'.

region.text: Aetolia and Triphylia

ledger.note: 217: the Peace of Naupactus ends the Social War; infobox 'Macedonian and Achaean victory'.

region.text: Bylazora, the Paeonian capital (identified with the Veles area; the page gives no location)

ledger.note: 217: Philip V takes Bylazora from the Dardani. 'he managed to capture Bylazora from them in 217 BCE' (Dardani page; the Dardani had taken it from the Paeonians in 230); the Paeonia page: 'In 217 BC, Philip V of Macedon incorporated into his empire Dassaretia and Paeonia by capturing Bylazora and the rest.' Mirrors kingdom-of-dardania; the Veles area is a reading.

region.text: the Illyrian coast from Oricum and Apollonia to Lissus

ledger.note: 214: the First Macedonian War opens in Illyria. 'In the late summer of 214 BC, Philip again attempted an Illyrian invasion by sea'; he took Oricum and besieged Apollonia; the fleet was lost.

region.text: Lissus and its citadel, and Dassaretis around Lake Ohrid

ledger.note: 213: Lissus falls. 'He was finally able to gain access to the Adriatic by capturing Lissus' (the Philip V page gives 212); 'Keeping clear of the coast, he took Dassaretis'. Lissus was 'the southernmost city of the Illyrian kingdom' (Gentius page).

region.text: 'Atintani and Parthini, and the town of Dimale', Roman client peoples since 228

ledger.note: 213-212: the Roman protectorate's interior taken. The Parthini and Atintani 'became Roman clients' in 228 (Illyrian Wars page). Place radii stand in for 'Parthini', 'Atintania' and 'Dimale', which the gazetteer lacks.

region.text: Oeniadae and Nasos

ledger.note: 211: Laevinus hands Oeniadae and Nasos to the Aetolians. 'the Acarnanian town of Oeniadae and the island of Nasos, which he handed over to the Aetolians' (First Macedonian War page). Oeniadae was taken by Philip in 219 (above) and held by Philip's Acarnanian allies; mirrors aetolian-league's 211 gain.

region.text: Anticyra in Phocis

ledger.note: 210: Anticyra to the Aetolians. 'Rome enslaved the inhabitants and Aetolia took possession of the town' (Phocian Anticyra, spring 210; the page names no previous holder, Livy says Locrian). Mirrors aetolian-league's 210 gain, which names this state; confidence 2 because the previous holder is the other dossier's reading.

region.text: Epicnemidian and Opuntian Locris (Thronium, Tithronium, Drymaea, Opus)

ledger.note: 208: Philip retakes the Locrian coast. 'He captured Thronium, followed by the towns of Tithronium and Drymaea north of the Cephisus' and 'attacked and took Opus' (First Macedonian War page; the years 209-208 are not separated, so 208 follows aetolian-league). Mirrors its 208 loss.

region.text: 'the Parthinians, Dimallum, Bargulum, and Eugenium', which 'Rome would control'

ledger.note: 205: the Peace of Phoenice. 'It was drawn up at Phoenice in 205 BC'; Macedon kept Atintania 'pending approval of the Senate of Rome'.

region.text: the Illyrian coast

ledger.note: 205: Phoenice ends the First Macedonian War ('stalemate and Peace of Phoenice').

region.text: Miletus, Samos and footholds in Caria (Iasos, Bargylia on the usual account)

ledger.note: 201: Philip in Asia Minor. 'Philip invaded their territories in Asia Minor', besieging Samos and capturing Miletus, and 'invaded Caria'; the navies 'clashed with Philip's off Chios and Lade (near Miletus) in 201 BC'. Samos was Ptolemaic; the Carian towns' owners (Rhodes, Ptolemy) are the researcher's reading.

region.text: the Illyrian and Epirote approaches (the Aous, 198), Upper Macedonia and Thessaly

ledger.note: 200: the Second Macedonian War (infobox 'March 200 - June 197 BC'). Abydos besieged 'in the autumn of 200 BC'; Sulpicius marched east 'In the spring of 199 BC'; the Aous (198) and Elateia captured.

region.text: Argos and the Argolid, taken over by Philokles

ledger.note: 198: Argos goes over to Philip. At the Achaean assembly at Sicyon 'The representatives of Argos, Megalopolis, and Dyme, which all had particularly strong ties with Philip, left the meeting', and 'From Corinth, Philokles was invited to take control of Argos by pro-Macedonians in the city, which he did without a fight' (Second Macedonian War page; the passage belongs to 198, no sentence gives the year). Argos had joined the Achaean League in 229 (above). The achaean-league dossier should record the loss.

region.text: Argos, handed to Nabis

ledger.note: Winter 198/197: Argos given to Nabis. 'Philip attempted to free up his forces by handing the city of Argos over to Nabis of Sparta' (Second Macedonian War page, 'the winter of 198/197' on the surrounding passage); Nabis later 'engineered a revolution in the city'. Placed in 197 to match peloponnesian-league's 197 gain.

region.text: Thessaly, decided at Cynoscephalae

ledger.note: June 197: Cynoscephalae. 'In June 197 BC, Flamininus marched north' and 'the legions of Flamininus defeated Philip's Macedonian phalanx'.

region.text: Thessaly, Magnesia, Perrhaebia and Phthiotic Achaea, whose peoples were proclaimed free

ledger.note: 196: the peace. 'Macedonia gives up all possessions and client states in Orestis, Thessaly, southern Greece, Thrace and Anatolia'; at the Isthmian Games of May 196 'the Corinthians, Phocians, Locrians, Euboeans, Magnesians, Thessalians, Perrhaebians, and the Phthiote Achaeans' were declared free. Thessaly had been Macedonian since 352; the freed leagues have no Cliopatria row (they fall inside Greek City-States).

region.text: 'the fetters of Greece, Demetrias, Chalcis, and Corinth', where 'Rome later kept garrisons'

ledger.note: 196: the fetters pass to Roman garrisons until 'the legions were not completely evacuated until 194 BC'; Corinth had 'earlier [been] promised... to the Achaeans'.

region.text: Orestis, the Carian footholds and the Thracian possessions

ledger.note: 196: Orestis freed and the Asian and Thracian garrisons withdrawn ('Philip had to remove all his garrisons in Greek cities in Europe and Asia, which were to be free and autonomous'). Orestis is the Kastoria-Grevena corner of Dytiki Makedonia, drawn here by the whole admin-1 unit for want of an 'Orestis' region.

region.text: Boeotia, freed with the other Greek states

ledger.note: 196: the Boeotians, Philip's allies at Phoenice (205), leave the Macedonian orbit with the proclamation of 'the Freedom of the Greeks'.

region.text: Demetrias and the Magnesian coast

ledger.note: 191: Macedon takes Demetrias from the Aetolians. 'The spring of 191 BC saw the Macedonians enter the war against the Aetolian League' (Roman-Seleucid war page); the Aetolians had seized Demetrias in 192 ('The Aetolians then moved troops to seize Sparta, Chalcis, and Demetrias', Aetolian League page: they succeeded only at Demetrias); the Philip V page lists Demetrias among what Rome let Philip keep (undated). Mirrors aetolian-league's 192 gain and 191 loss.

region.text: 'a number of towns in Thessaly', read as the Larissa plain

ledger.note: 191: Macedon occupies Thessalian towns. 'occupy a number of towns in Thessaly' (Roman-Seleucid war page, 191). The towns belonged to the Roman-protected Thessalian League (freed in 196, above), not to the Aetolian League; the Larissa disc is a reading. Surrendered again c. 185.

region.text: parts of Athamania, Dolopia and Perrhaebia that 'Rome let Philip keep'; the Ioanina radius stands for Athamania's eastern part

ledger.note: 191: Athamanian lands. The Philip V page lists what Rome let Philip keep without dates; Athamania (a kingdom allied to the Aetolians, no Cliopatria row, no dossier) is a separate owner from the Aetolian League. Confidence 1: year bridged from the 191 campaign.

region.text: the Thessalian towns given up at Rome's demand

ledger.note: c. 185: the Thessalian towns of 191 surrendered. No page opened dates this (the Roman commission of 185/184 on the usual account); Cliopatria's 170 shape (43,431 km2) has lost them. Demetrias and the Magnesian coast stayed Macedonian on the usual account; the page is silent.

region.text: the Athamanian towns given up at Rome's demand

ledger.note: c. 185: the Athamanian lands of 191 surrendered (undated on the pages opened; same bridge as the Thessalian towns).

region.text: Thessaly (Callinicus, 171) and the Epirote and Illyrian borderlands

ledger.note: 171: the Third Macedonian War (infobox 171-168). Callinicus (171) 'inconclusive'; Perseus besieged Uscana and ravaged Illyrian towns in 169.

region.text: the Molossians of Epirus, who 'went over to the Macedonians'

ledger.note: 170: the Molossians join Perseus. 'Molossians in Epirus, on the west coast of Greece, went over to the Macedonians' (170 BC); Cliopatria's Molossians row (170-165) is their breakaway from the Epirote League, polities/molossians.json.

region.text: the Molossians

ledger.note: 168: the Molossian alliance ends with Pydna; in 167 Roman troops 'were sent to seventy cities' of Epirus and '150,000 people were enslaved'.

region.text: Thessaly and the Macedonian frontier

ledger.note: 22 June 168: Pydna. Infobox '22 June 168 BC', 'Roman victory; Fall of Macedon'; 'Perseus fled with the cavalry on the Macedonian right' and 'later surrendered to Paullus'.

region.text: Macedon, 'divided into four merides' with capitals at Amphipolis, Thessalonica, Pella and Pelagonia

ledger.note: 168: the Antigonid kingdom ends at Pydna; 'the Antigonid kingdom was dissolved and replaced by four republics' (Perseus page). The 167 settlement: 'Macedon was to be divided into four merides', tribute 'half of what the king had received', 'Gold and silver mines were not allowed to be mined'; the province of Macedonia follows Andriscus's defeat (148) in 146.

wars.name: Fourth War of the Diadochi (Ipsus)
wars.outcome: 'Antigonid defeat' (Diadochi infobox): Antigonus killed at Ipsus (301); his kingdom 'carved up between the victors', Lysimachus taking western Asia Minor, Seleucus the east and Syria; Demetrius kept his fleet, Cyprus and Greek cities. Rhodes withstood the siege: 'in 304 BC after only one year, he relented and signed a peace agreement'.

wars.name: Demetrius's wars in Greece and Macedon
wars.outcome: Athens and the Macedonian throne taken in 294; Boeotia resecured in 291; in 288 Pyrrhus, Ptolemy and Lysimachus 'obliged him to leave Macedonia' and divided it.

wars.name: Gallic invasion and the Battle of Lysimachia

zones.text: Macedon, overrun by Bolgios and Brennus in 279

wars.outcome: 'In 277 BC, Antigonus II Gonatas defeated the Gauls at the Battle of Lysimachia' and 'claim[ed] the Macedonian throne'; the survivors founded Tyle in Thrace and others crossed to Asia as the Galatians.

wars.name: Pyrrhus's invasion of Macedon
wars.outcome: Pyrrhus 'seized the Macedonian throne from Antigonus II Gonatas in 274 BC and invaded the Peloponnese in 272 BC'; killed 'during a street battle at Argos' in 272, after which his army surrendered to Antigonus.

wars.name: Chremonidean War
wars.outcome: 'Macedonian victory' that 'confirmed Antigonid control over Greece': Athens garrisoned; the Ptolemaic fleet 'defeated off Cos (probably in 261 BC)'.

wars.name: Revolt of Alexander of Corinth
wars.outcome: Corinth recovered 'in the winter of 245/44 BC'; the start year is not on the page.

wars.name: Demetrian War
wars.outcome: 'It was only during the reign of Demetrios II (239-229) that Aitolia and Macedonia were at war' (Aetolian League page); Boeotia submitted (236); Agron's Illyrians relieved Medion (232/231); 'the Dardani defeated Demetrius who died shortly the next spring' (229); Athens and Argos left the Macedonian orbit in 229.

wars.name: Cleomenean War (Macedonian intervention)

zones.text: Arcadia: Mantinea, Heraea, Telphusa 223; Megalopolis sacked

wars.outcome: 'Achaean and Macedonian victory'; 'Acrocorinth, Corinth, Heraea, and Orchomenus went to Macedon'; Antigonus entered Sparta but did not force it into his league; Cleomenes fled to Egypt.

wars.name: Social War (220-217 BC)
wars.outcome: 'Macedonian and Achaean victory'; the Peace of Naupactus (217) on the principle 'that every side should maintain what it currently possessed'; 'Triphylia and Phthiotis went to Macedon, while Psophis and Lasion went to Achaea'.

wars.name: First Macedonian War

zones.text: Anticyra, taken by Rome and the Aetolians 210
Oeniadae and Nasos handed to the Aetolians; Thermon raided c. 207

wars.outcome: 'stalemate and Peace of Phoenice' (205): Rome 'would control the Parthinians, Dimallum, Bargulum, and Eugenium', Macedon kept Atintania; the Aetolians had made a separate peace in 206; Aegina was sold to Attalus.

wars.name: Philip V's Aegean and Carian campaign (Cretan War)
wars.outcome: Miletus captured and Caria invaded (201); the fleets 'clashed with Philip's off Chios and Lade' (201); the Rhodians 'appealed in 201 BC to the Roman Republic'; the Asian footholds were given up in 196.

wars.name: Second Macedonian War
wars.outcome: Roman victory: 'Macedonia gives up all possessions and client states in Orestis, Thessaly, southern Greece, Thrace and Anatolia', pays 1,000 talents and surrenders 'his whole navy except for his flagship'; 'Freedom of the Greeks' proclaimed at the Isthmian Games of May 196; Rome evacuates in 194.

wars.name: Roman-Seleucid War (Macedon on the Roman side)
wars.outcome: Antiochus beaten at Thermopylae (191); the Macedonians 'occupy a number of towns in Thessaly'; Rome let Philip keep Demetrias, the Magnesian coast and parts of Athamania, Dolopia and Perrhaebia for a time.

wars.name: Third Macedonian War
wars.outcome: 'Roman victory': Pydna (22 June 168); Perseus surrendered at Samothrace; Macedon 'divided into four merides' (167); Epirus sacked ('150,000 people were enslaved'); Gentius's Illyria 'split into three cantons'.

certainty.note: Approximate frontiers throughout: the Illyrian, Dardanian and Thracian borders of Macedon, the limits of the garrison-held Greek districts, and the satrapal lines of 306-301. The 196 and 167 Roman settlements name peoples, not surveyed lines.

notes:
One dossier for two Cliopatria rows: 'Antigonid Dynasty' (-291..-278) and 'Antigonid Macedonia' (-277..-165) share Wikidata Q237325 and are one continuous state, the Antigonid house's kingdom (Demetrius's Macedon 294-288, Gonatas's Greek garrisons 288-277, Macedon 277-168). The dossier is started in 306 (Antigonus's royal title) so that Antigonus's kingdom of Asia, which Cliopatria draws inside its 'Macedonian Empire' shape of 307-302, has an owner in its own colour; that is a new keyframe at confidence 2, and the 301-295 keyframe (Demetrius's Cyprus and Corinth) is at confidence 1. The reviewer may instead start the dossier in 294 and leave Antigonus's Asia inside the Macedonian Empire row; either way the two Antigonid rows should be merged.

Cliopatria rows to correct (keyframe_review): the Antigonid row begins 291 (Demetrius took Macedon in 294) and keeps Macedon to 285 although Lysimachus and Pyrrhus held it from 288/287; the 256-248 shape reaches 19.2 E (the Epirote/Illyrian coast) without any gain the pages record; the 197-171 shape reaches 29.6 E (Aenus and Maronea in Thrace, which Philip held after 190 on the usual account; no page opened says so); the kingdom ends June 168, not 165. Macedon under Ptolemy Keraunos, Meleager, Antipater Etesias and Sosthenes (281-277) has no Cliopatria shape at all: a short dossier (suggested slug macedon-281-277 or ptolemy-keraunos) or an extension of the Lysimachus row is needed; see the notes file.

States Cliopatria lacks that this dossier's counterparts need: Epirus (polities/kingdom-of-epirus.json, written by another batch of this group), the Chremonidean coalition (polities/chremonidean-alliance.json), Sparta under Cleomenes III and Nabis (counterpart 'Sparta (Cleomenes III)'; a Sparta dossier is listed under counterparts_needing_dossiers), the Boeotian League, the Thessalian League and the other leagues freed in 196, Athamania, the Dardani, Alexander of Corinth's breakaway (c. 253-245), Tyle. Athens is drawn inside Cliopatria's Greek City-States row; the vassal tints over Attica (322-307, 261-229) are addressed to greek-city-states.

Disagreements between pages: Demetrius expelled from Macedon 288 (Demetrius page, Macedonia page) or 287 (Lysimachus page), his reign in Macedon 294-288 (text) or 294-287 (dynasty table); Pyrrhus driven out 284 (Pyrrhus page) or 285 (Lysimachus page); Antigonus Gonatas king of Macedon from 277 (Lysimachia, Gonatas infobox) or 276 (dynasty table); Lissus taken 213 (First Macedonian War page) or 212 (Philip V page); Athens surrendered 262 or 261; the Cleomenean War page does not date Argos's and Corinth's defection to Cleomenes (225) or the Acrocorinth handover (224).

Gaps a gap-filler should fill: the 330s-301 Asian satrapies are the me-05 group's; Demetrius's holdings 301-294 ('Demetrius I of Macedon' sections or 'Ptolemy I Soter' for Cyprus 294); Thessaly's status 288-277; Alexander of Corinth's start year; the 185/184 surrender of the Thessalian and Athamanian towns and the Thracian cities Aenus and Maronea ('Philip V of Macedon' is silent); Perseus's Illyrian conquests of 169 (Uscana) as occupations; Macedon's own area in any year (no infobox figure on the Antigonid or Macedonia pages for this period).

Fix run of 2026-10-19 (after the adversarial review). Changed: mirrors added for the Aetolian events of 211, 210 and 208 (First Macedonian War), 303 (Polyperchon), 275 (Aegium, Achaean League), 227 (southern Paeonia), 217 (Bylazora), 219 (Oeniadae and Elaeus) and 198-197 (Argos: gain from the Achaean League, loss to Nabis); the 219 Triphylia gain is recentred south of the Alpheus (Zacharo and Lepreon) and names Elis, not the Aetolian League; the 191 gain is split by owner (Demetrias from the Aetolians, the Thessalian towns from the Thessalian League, Athamanian lands from Athamania) and the c. 185 loss likewise; the 306-302 keyframe now ends in 305 and the new -304 keyframe adds Corinth, Boeotia and Euboea; Boeotia is dropped from the 301-295 keyframe (ledger loss c. 301 at confidence 1, regained 291); Cyprus is lost to Ptolemy in 294 (Ptolemy I Soter page 'reconquered Cyprus in 295/294'); North Macedonia is dropped from the Epirote regions of 288, 274 and 272 (Paeonia was independent); the Thessaly loss of 288 names kingdom-of-epirus (Pyrrhus page) instead of Lysimachus. Already applied by the reviewer: the 288 loss to Lysimachus names Kentriki Makedonia, and the war of 307 starts in 306.
Counterparts to fix elsewhere: achaean-league should record the 198 loss of Argos to this state (it has the 229 gain and the 197 return, but not 198); kingdom-of-epirus should record the Thessaly gain (288 here, bridged; 286 on the page) and its 285 loss to Lysimachus; ptolemaic-kingdom should record the 294 gain of Cyprus; polyperchon, aetolian-league and kingdom-of-dardania already carry the other side of the new mirrors; 'Elis' (219) and 'Athamania' (191) have no dossier.
